National Population Policy
*261. SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the policy laid down by the National
Commission on Population towards a stable
and sustainable population size;
(b) whether it is a fact that the National
Population Policy (NPP) desires to bring
the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) to the
replacement level of  2.10 by the year 2010;
(c) whether it would be possible with this
TFR of 2.10, to restrict the National Population
to 1107 million by 2010 A.D.; and
(d) whether it is also a fact that the
Planning Commission has set a target of
population growth of 16.2 per cent between
2001 and 2011 in the Tenth Five Year Plan,
implying a population of 1193 million?
Ban on Pakistani newspapers
*262. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a continued mutual
ban in India and Pakistan on each other's
newspapers; and
(b) whether as a logical follow-up of
Delhi-Lahore Bus Service and restoration
of airline flights between India and Pakistan,
India would take the initiative in lifting the
ban on Pakistani newspapers?
Rail link between New Delhi and
Hanoi
*263. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Myanmar
Foreign Minister, at a recent meeting of
Mekong-Ganga Cooperation Group held
at Phnom Penh, made a proposal for a rail
link between New Delhi and Hanoi;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(c) whether any agency has been
identified for conducting feasibility study
of the project; if so, the details thereof?
Settlement of labour disputes through
teleconferencing
*264. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of LABOUR be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
an IT company is developing a software to
settlement of labour disputes in Delhi
throught teleconferencing; if so, the details
thereof; and

2
(b) whether any all-India level study
has been made to find out the average time
taken to settle labour disputes and if so,
the details thereof?
Closure of industrial establishment
*265. SHRI GAYA SINGH:
SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of LABOUR be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of closures lock-out, lay-
off and retrenchments the industrial
establishments reported during the period
2001-02 and 2002-03 and the number of
workers affected, State-wise; and
(b) the reasons therefor?
Mobile services in Jharkhand
†*266.  SHRI VIJAY SINGH YADAV:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Sanchar
Nigam or any other company has not yet
succeeded in launching mible services in
Dakara (Ranchi), Jharkhand;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether any efforts have been made
so far to launch mobile services in this
town, if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) by when the Sanchar Nigam is likely
to launch the said sarvices in the area?
Superfast highway connection
between India and China
*267. SHRI K. NATWAR SINGH:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether a superfast highway
connecting India with uts neighbours in the
East was discussed during the Prime
Minister's visit besides opening border trade
with Beijing via Sikkim;
(b) if so, to what extent Myanmar,
Bhutan and Bangladesh;
(c) whether Indian had sought to
complete this highway project within 36
months of announcing it in 2001; if so, the
reasons for delay; and
(d) by when this highway link is likely
to be completed?
Unemployment problem
*268. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of LABOUR be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the avenues
for employment are SHRInking and the
number of unemployed and semi-employed
persons are soaring over the years;
(b) the generation of employment
opportunities planned in different
categories during the period 2003-04 and
2004-05;
(c) what has been and what is likely to
be the impact of cut in jobs in Government
PSUs divestment in PSUs and closure of
industrial units in creating new job
opportunities; and
(d) whether Government have set any
target to provide employment to every
eligible citizen of the country?

Industrialisation in Uttar Pradesh
1923. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the present status of the National
Programmes on Rural Industrialisation in
the industrially backward districts of Uttar
Pradesh; and
(b) the details of achievements made,
so far, in this regard?
Scheme for Cottage Industries
†1924. SHRI ABHAY KANT
PRASAD: Will the Minister of AGRO
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
prepare any scheme for the promotion of
Cottage Industries in the rural areas of the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the allocation of funds
made by Government for the promotion of
Cottage Industries during the year 2002-03,
State-wise?
Land to displaced Adivasis
1925. SHRI AIMADUDDIN
AHMAD KHAN (DURRU): Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether necessary compensations
including alternative land have since been
provided to those Adivasis who were
displaced from their home land (Trombay
village) at Trombay Hills which was
acquired for the construction of
multistoried building for BARC's
employees;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) by when, the whole process of
settlement of the displaced Adivasis would
be finalised?
Impact of radiation on workers
1926. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the high radiation which has affected
adversely on workers engaged in various
atomic power plants in the country;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

421
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have chalked
out any strategy to deal with the situation;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Waiting-list of telephone
connections in J&K
1927. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of persons on waiting-
list for telephone connections in Jammu
and Kashmir as on the 31st March, 2003;
(b) whether any time-frame has been
fixed for clearance of the wait-listed
applications; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
clear the backlog?
C.A.G.'s  revelation  on  short-
comings of MTNL services
1928. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
performance review by the Comptroller and
Auditor General of India on the quality
services provided by the MTNL has
revealed several shortcomings;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what action is taken/proposed to be
taken to rectify such shortcomings?
Collaboration by MIT Media Lab
1929. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Massachusetts Institute
of Technology Media Lab has pulled out
of collaboration in India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of agreement for entering
into the collaboration;
(d) the details of projects established in
the country by this arrangement;
(e) the total expenditure incurred by
Government and other parties separately;
and
(f) the present status of these
projects?
Monsoon Hangama Offer of a
private operator
1930. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Cellular Operators
Association of India has complained to DoT
on the fraudulent intentions of Monsoon
Hangama Offer of a private operator to
deceive the subscriber with misleading
features of the scheme;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the COAI fears that the
Monsoon Hangama Offer might influence
the forthcoming decision of TDS Appellate
Tribunal on the legality of WLL Mobility
Services; and
(d) whether the operator owes to the
DoT a staggering sum of Rs. 9000 crore as

422
unpaid licence fee?
Disrupted telecommunication
system in Ranchi

negligence of the officers of
Telecommunication Department, the
communication system of Dakra (Ranchi)
generally remains disrupted;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
telephones of many Central Educational
Institutions are also lying out of order since
the last six months due to non-presence of
officers/employees at the headquarters;
(c) by when the faulty telephone
